newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit extends losses in Europe on shortcovering.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit extends losses in Europe on shortcovering.

text.p: The ringgit fell further in early Europe as funds continued covering their short dollar and Singapore dollar positions, dealers said on Wednesday.

They said long ringgit positions were being unwound due to the dollar's strength against other major currencies and Singapore Finance Minister's comments in an interview seeking a stronger Singapore dollar.
"It is difficult to maintain long ringgit positions in the face of a surging dollar," one Malaysian bank dealer said.
He said U.S. funds were the main sellers of the regional currencies.
Dealers said comments by Singapore Finance Minister Richard Hu in an interview with the Financial Times had triggered a panic return of funds to the Singapore dollar.
Hu was quoted as saying that some strengthening of the Singapore dollar would be desirable to keep inflation down.
"There is a lot of long ringgit and short Sing positions in the market, which are being covered," said a dealer with a European bank in Singapore.
At 1130 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.4980/90 a dollar, after touching a low of 2.50 earlier, and at 1.7738/57 a Singapore dollar. -- Madhav Reddy (603-230 8911)
